inputs.name: openbao_version
inputs.description: OpenBao release to install, without the leading v.

inputs.name: checksums
inputs.description: SHA-256 of the linux_amd64 and linux_arm64 release tarballs, keyed x86_64 and aarch64, from the release's checksums.txt. Change these with openbao_version.

inputs.name: listen_address
inputs.description: Address the API listens on. The default keeps OpenBao to the host itself. Any address other than loopback needs tls_cert_file and tls_key_file.

inputs.name: api_port
inputs.description: Port of the API and UI. The cluster port, which raft uses, is the next one up.

inputs.name: tls_cert_file
inputs.description: Path on the host of the listener's certificate, in PEM, with any intermediates after it. When null, the listener runs plain HTTP, which only a loopback listen_address allows. The openbao user must be able to read it.

inputs.name: tls_key_file
inputs.description: Path on the host of the listener's private key, in PEM. The openbao user must be able to read it.

inputs.name: ui
inputs.description: Serve the web UI on the API port, at /ui.

inputs.name: initialize
inputs.description: Initialise OpenBao on the first apply with one unseal key, and write the key and root token to /root/openbao-init.json, mode 0600. For labs and homelabs only: the key sits on the same disk as the data it protects. When false, run bao operator init yourself.

inputs.name: seal
inputs.description: Auto-unseal: a seal type, such as "transit" or "awskms", and its settings, written into a seal stanza in the config. The config and the plan show the settings, so pass tokens and credentials in environment instead. When null, OpenBao uses unseal keys.

inputs.name: environment
inputs.description: Environment variables for the OpenBao server, such as BAO_TOKEN for a transit seal or a password a self_init request reads with eval_source = "env". Written to /etc/openbao/openbao.env, mode 0600; it never reaches state or the plan. Needs seal.

inputs.name: self_init
inputs.description: OpenBao's self-initialisation: a list of initialize blocks, each with a name and a list of requests, each request with a name, operation and path and optionally data, token and allow_failure. They run once, in order, on the first start. Needs seal; not with initialize.
